title: Israel announces a complete siege of the Gaza Strip
body:
On 9 October 2023, two days after the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, Israeli Defence Minister Yoav Gallant announced a complete siege of the Gaza Strip. In a video statement he said: "We are putting a complete siege on Gaza. No electricity, no food, no water, no gas, it's all closed." He said Israel was fighting human animals and acting accordingly.

About 2.3 million people live in Gaza, one of the most densely populated areas in the world. Israel had blockaded the territory in its current form since June 2007, controlling its airspace, territorial waters and two of its three border crossings; Egypt controls the third, at Rafah. The new measures went beyond that existing blockade by cutting electricity and halting the entry of food and fuel.

The same day, Israeli military spokesperson Rear Admiral Daniel Hagari said Israel had regained control of its communities near the border after the Hamas incursion, and that 15 of 24 border communities had been evacuated, with the rest expected to follow within 24 hours. A Hamas spokesperson, Abdel-Latif al-Qanoua, told the Associated Press that Hamas fighters were still fighting outside Gaza and had captured more Israelis that morning, and that the group sought the release of all Palestinian prisoners held by Israel. The siege was widely criticised by UN officials and humanitarian organisations as collective punishment, and the supply of electricity, fuel and water remained a central issue in the following months.
